title: Cycle Surge Buffer & Conditional Scope Pause Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a lightweight operational playbook that pre-allocates a cycle-level surge buffer and defines an automated, conditional scope pause mechanism. The goal is to avoid mid-cycle panic cuts while preserving capacity for critical incidents and high-impact scope that emerges after planning. This playbook will standardize signals, ownership, and communications for reserving and releasing surge lanes.
context: Repeated mid-cycle firefighting has led to ad-hoc scope cuts and uneven cross-team reassignments
Existing capacity playbooks focus on manual tranche decisions; we need an automated gating layer tied to measured signals
Customers and enterprise roadmaps require higher predictability for Dedicated/Private feature launches
We want a small, repeatable process teams can opt into that reduces decision friction and improves fairness of staffing rotations
proposed_solution: Reserve 8% of cycle engineering points as two 'surge lanes' (one for incidents/P0 and one for emergent high-impact scope). Surge lanes are not allocated to squads at sprint start and are staffed by a rotating pool.

Create an automated gating service (simple dashboard + webhook) that evaluates three signals hourly: remaining committed capacity, active P0/P1 incident load, and downstream launch blockers flagged by Product/PMs.

If gating thresholds are crossed, the service emits a 'conditional pause' signal which triggers the governance runbook: pause all non-critical tickets marked 'stretch' and divert the rotating pool to the surge lane for a 3-5 day window.
Implement a transparent ledger (spreadsheet + console dashboard) that tracks surge lane usage, reassignments, and compensation adjustments for teams that loan engineers.
Document handoff templates and notifications for engineering leads, product managers, and design when a surge lane is activated or released.
Run a 2-cycle pilot with 3 cross-functional pods and iterate thresholds and rotation cadence based on measured outcomes (customer impact, velocity variance, team satisfaction).
triggers_and_thresholds: Primary trigger: Cycle committed capacity remaining <= 14% AND projected sprint capacity deficit >= 1 engineer-week
Secondary trigger: More than 1 rolling P0 incident active for >24 hours or a single P0 impacting customer SLAs
Tertiary trigger: Blocker flagged by >1 PM for an enterprise launch with release date within 10 working days
Manual override: VP Product or Head of Eng can trigger or cancel surge lane activation after convening the governance panel

Release condition: surge lane active period ends after 3 business days if cumulative incident time drops below threshold and projected capacity gap is closed; can be extended once with documented rationale
roles_and_responsibilities: Cycle Capacity Owner (Product Manager): monitors dashboard, authorizes pilot activations when automated signal recommends
Engineering Rotation Lead (Eng Manager): assembles rotation pool, issues assignments, and tracks time charged to surge ledger
Incident Commander (on-call engineer): owns P0 triage while surge lane engineers execute mitigation tasks
Design Liaison: prioritizes critical UX fixes and pauses non-essential design tasks during surge
Communications Owner: sends standardized notifications to org, updates roadmap tracker and customer comms if needed
acceptance_criteria: Pilot completed across 3 pods for two cycles with documented activations and releases
Dashboard reflects real-time gating signals and shows historical surge lane events
Rotation ledger is populated for each activation and shows time reallocated per engineer and team
Post-pilot retrospective shows <=10% net negative impact on committed roadmap velocity for participating pods and improved time-to-resolution for P0 incidents
Clear handoff/playbook docs exist and are linked in the cycle kickoff checklist
